stories.headline: Babiš meets Zelensky in Yerevan on sidelines of European Political Community summit
stories.summary: Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Yerevan on May 3, the first meeting between the two leaders since Babiš returned to office in December. The talks, held the day before the EPC summit, covered bilateral relations, energy (including Kazakh gas transit via Ukraine), and Ukraine's path to EU membership; Babiš said the key question for peace is finding a mediator, floating Central Asian leaders and Erdoğan as possibilities.

stories.headline: Czech PM leads major Central Asia and South Caucasus trade mission; energy and defense deals signed
stories.summary: Between April 26–30, Prime Minister Babiš led a business delegation of ~50 companies through Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan, accompanied by Deputy PM Karel Havlíček. Key outcomes included advanced gas supply negotiations with CEZ/Azerbaijan, six cooperation memorandums with Kazakhstan, and a bilateral trade target of $1 billion with Uzbekistan. The visit also included Czech defense group CSG announcing a joint venture with an Azerbaijani partner for servicing armored vehicles, and coverage of the Czech arms industry's record revenues approaching 180 billion CZK.

stories.headline: Babiš appoints ex-NATO ambassador Landovský as envoy amid dispute over Czech defense spending compliance
stories.summary: Prime Minister Babiš announced on May 1 that former Czech ambassador to NATO Jakub Landovský would become a government envoy for meeting NATO commitments, after admitting the Czech Republic would not reach the 2% GDP defense spending target in 2026. The announcement triggered opposition mockery and an ongoing fact-check controversy about whether Babiš is correct that even the previous Fiala government missed the threshold under the new NATO methodology. President Pavel and Defense Minister Zůna also publicly criticized the shortfall.

stories.headline: Czech National Bank Governor Michl argues for Bitcoin allocation in sovereign reserves at Las Vegas conference
stories.summary: CNB Governor Aleš Michl spoke at the Bitcoin 2026 conference in Las Vegas on April 28, making the case for a ~1% Bitcoin allocation in the CNB's $180 billion reserve portfolio based on internal research showing improved risk-adjusted returns. He acknowledged Bitcoin's extreme volatility and said it 'honestly looks too risky,' but framed a small allocation as prudent diversification; the bank has already run a small experimental digital-asset test portfolio.

stories.headline: Okamura visits Belgrade, meets Vučić and Brnabić; calls Czech recognition of Kosovo a mistake
stories.summary: Czech parliamentary speaker and SPD leader Tomio Okamura made an official visit to Serbia around April 29–30, meeting President Vučić and National Assembly President Brnabić. Okamura expressed support for Serbia's EU integration, called Prague's recognition of Kosovo a failure of past Czech politicians, and said he personally considers Kosovo to be Serbia. The visit generated extensive coverage in Serbian media and drew reaction in Czech media.

stories.headline: Babiš-Pavel-Macinka standoff over who leads Czech delegation at July NATO Ankara summit
stories.summary: A constitutional dispute has developed between President Petr Pavel and the Babiš government over who will represent the Czech Republic at the NATO summit in Ankara in July. Pavel insists on leading the delegation as is traditional; Babiš has said it should be himself; Foreign Minister Macinka (Motorists) has publicly dismissed Pavel's claim and called it part of a re-election campaign. Pavel's adviser has signaled a possible competency lawsuit if the government blocks the president. The two are scheduled to meet on May 8.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Babiš has repeatedly and publicly criticized Filip Turek, the government's climate envoy from Motorists, for continued inflammatory rhetoric (calling civil servants 'parasites') after entering government. Babiš said in a television appearance that Turek 'would not be a minister' under his management, and accused Motorists generally of not understanding they are now in government. Commentators interpret this as Babiš strategically positioning ANO as the responsible party while coalition partners generate controversy.

stories.headline: SPD gives pro-Russia statements to Kremlin-linked Izvestia; coalition faces accusations of collaboration
stories.summary: Three SPD politicians, including MP Zuzana Majerová, gave statements to the Russian state-aligned newspaper Izvestia regarding the possibility of restoring Czech-Russian diplomatic ties. Opposition labeled the SPD figures 'collaborators' and compared the statements to the 1968 invitation letter. Separately, SPD speaker Okamura publicly stated he would block weapons purchases for Ukraine, and the party's deputy defense minister reportedly obstructed the Czech munitions initiative. Babiš has not distanced himself from SPD despite the controversy.

stories.headline: Petr Fiala (former PM) increases social media presence; ODS colleague floats presidential candidacy
stories.summary: Former Prime Minister Petr Fiala has sharply increased his social media activity since leaving government, posting informal videos including a garden tractor clip. An ODS vice-chairman publicly said he could 'imagine Fiala as president,' the first explicit statement from party leadership since Fiala said in January he would not run in 2028. Separately, Fiala and Czech-Budějovice governor Martin Kuba exchanged barbs on social media in a sign of internal ODS tension.

Policy documents on hybrid threats and NATO readiness were also published by the Czech defence think-tank community.

stories.summary: Senate President Miloš Vystrčil (ODS) accused Prime Minister Babiš of revenge by refusing to provide a government aircraft for his delegation's official visit to Taiwan. Vystrčil said the decision would harm Czech businesses and researchers; Babiš's government cited the 'one China' policy. Vystrčil linked Babiš's attitude to jealousy over Czech-Taiwan cooperation developed under the previous government.
